summary: Unexpected final-token drop when client applies aggressive flow-control during WebSocket upgrade
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed consistent loss of the last token/terminal choice when a streaming session is established via WebSocket upgrade through their in-house reverse proxy. The symptom happens only when the HyperWriter client toggles an aggressive read/pause policy (client-side flow control) during the initial transcript flush immediately after the 101 Switching Protocols handshake.

Impact:
- Affected customer reports truncated completions in production for ~8% of WebSocket sessions during peak load which results in user-visible sentence truncation.
- Requests are otherwise served (no 5xx), but final token or trailing punctuation is missing.
- Customer uses Dedicated capacity and observed only in us-east region behind their proxy appliance.

Why this ticket exists:
- Reproducible in customer environment and intermittently in our internal staging when a synthetic proxy is injected. We need to determine where the terminal tokens are being dropped (client suspend/read, proxy buffer close, or server-side flush race) and provide a mitigation and long-term fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer establishes HTTP connection to API endpoint through their reverse proxy configured to perform WebSocket upgrades (Upgrade: websocket).
2) Client sends a streaming-completion request with streaming=true and opens WebSocket after 101 response. Payload contains long completion with clear terminal punctuation expectation.
3) Immediately after upgrade, client-side SDK toggles aggressive flow control: pauses reading frames for 50-120ms (simulated in SDK by setting read buffer to zero/toggle event loop).

4) Observe server-side stream completes generation and sends final-choice frames, but client application sometimes never receives the last token or receives stream close with no terminal choice event.
5) Repeat under bursty load (100 concurrent streams) and the failure rate increases to ~6-10%.
logs: [client-sdk] 2026-03-01T14:12:02Z pause_read: flow control engaged, delay_ms=80, session_id=svc-8b3d
[streaming-runtime] 2026-03-01T14:12:02Z write-confirmation-missing: final_choice not acknowledged within 120ms, session_id=svc-8b3d
investigation_notes: Edge probe: reproduces at ~6% when synthetic proxy configured to buffer upgrade traffic and apply a short drain timeout (50-120ms).

Server-side: runtime emits final-choice event and marks stream as completed; internal ack to connection layer logged but not always confirmed before connection soft-close by proxy. No model-side truncation observed in generation logs.

Client-side: when the SDK pauses reading, it does not ack frame receipts to the socket layer which allows the proxy to consider the downstream connection idle and trigger a soft-close during its buffer-drain window.
Network traces: TLS-level records show final bytes cross network, but WebSocket frame assembly on client sometimes missing last control metadata (end-of-choice marker) when pause latency > ~60ms.
Staging replication: introducing an artificial 75ms read pause in our internal SDK + simple proxy reproduces the missing-final-token symptom consistently.
No evidence of model generation stopping early; captured model logits show full sequence emitted.
hypothesis: The root cause is a race between the streaming-runtime's flush of the terminal choice and the customer's proxy 'buffer-drain' soft-close policy. When the client-side SDK pauses reads, the proxy interprets the lack of downstream reads as idle and closes the connection before the proxy has drained frames into the WebSocket forwarding pipeline, dropping the final choice. In short: flow-control pause -> proxy drain timeout -> proxy soft-close racing with runtime flush acknowledgement.
workaround: Short-term: ask HyperWriter to increase proxy drain timeout to >250ms and disable aggressive client-side read pauses. Alternatively, enable 'buffered-resume' on the client SDK (experimental flag) so it reads frames continuously but stalls processing at application layer.
resolution_notes: Investigation ongoing. Proposed immediate mitigation pushed to customer: extend proxy drain timeout and enable SDK buffered-read. Engineering to evaluate adding an extra connection-level handshake acknowledgement for terminal-choice frames to avoid proxy early-close races.
next_steps: 1) Engineering (streaming-runtime) to prototype a short 'terminal-ack' control frame that ensures the transport layer doesn't consider the session 'complete' until the client-side stack has seen and acked the final-choice event.
2) Client SDK team to expose a 'read-backpressure-tolerance-ms' config that defaults to a conservative value for Dedicated customers behind proxies.
3) SRE to add a synthetic test to the staging suite that reproduces this proxy+pause race to prevent regressions.
4) Follow up with HyperWriter on 2026-03-04 to confirm whether the proxy config change reduces failure rate.
comments: 2026-03-01 15:03 - Liam Chen: Assigned. Collected traces from HyperWriter and reproduced locally with synthetic proxy. Initial suspicion is proxy drain race, see investigation notes.
2026-03-01 16:20 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed increasing drain timeout to 300ms reduced failures from ~8% to <1%. They can apply as interim fix but prefer a server-side hardening.
2026-03-02 09:12 - Marco Ruiz (streaming-runtime): Looking at introducing a lightweight terminal ACK on the WebSocket control channel. Will spike this week and provide an impact estimate.
2026-03-03 11:44 - SRE Oncall: Added synthetic test to staging that simulates SDK read-pause; CI failing intentionally until fix merged to avoid regressions.
